title: Peas and carrots, fresh, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Peas and carrots are popular vegetables often combined in cooking. In this version they are fresh, boiled and prepared with added fat, which enhances flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas belong to the legume family and are rich in plant protein, while carrots are root vegetables high in beta‑carotene.
Traditionally in Russian cuisine peas and carrots are cooked together in soups and stews.
A small amount of vegetable oil increases the bioavailability of carotenoids from carrots.
The combination provides a broad spectrum of amino acids, complementing each other.
Both vegetables can be stored in the refrigerator for up to a week, but are best enjoyed fresh.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A to support vision and immunity.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Added vegetable fat (e.g., olive oil) supplies monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Both vegetables contain fiber that promotes healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Carotenoids and flavonoids in carrots and peas help combat free radicals.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Excessive fat intake
items.content: Too much added fat raises the calorie density of the dish.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions of peas can cause gas in sensitive people.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Carrots contain modest amounts of oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stones in predisposed individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish, add to salads, soups, or stews. Garnish with fresh herbs or a squeeze of lemon juice for brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in a pan with a little oil to retain texture.
